title: Protocols for Flexible Data Sources
hints: Two small protocols, combined into one requirement with `&`.
`typealias ButtonDataSourceProtocol = ButtonTextProtocol & ButtonPressedProtocol`, then inject it into `ScreenModel`.
jsBridge: Injecting a protocol-typed dependency into a view model is TS "program to an interface", constructor-injecting `ButtonTextProvider`. Swift's nominal protocols make the seams explicit, and mocks become tiny structs.

compass.q: In TS you might just pass an object literal matching the interface. In Swift you need a type that declares conformance. Is that friction worth it?
How would you swap a real data service for a mock in SwiftUI previews using this pattern?
Protocol injection vs closure injection (`let fetch: () async -> [Item]`): which is lighter for small dependencies?
`any ButtonTextProtocol` vs a generic `ViewModel<T: ButtonTextProtocol>`: what changes for performance and flexibility?
